answers.answer: Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for 3–4 players. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next-numbered in Section B, then alternate A/B; all begin Locked-side up. Put in the bag 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 4 additional Adults (one per player), for 7 Adults total.
answers.evidence: Setup, board steps 7 and 10: '3 for 3–4 players'; lowest-numbered pod in A then B, alternating; all pods Locked; bag contents include 3 Adults plus 1 Adult per player.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards marked for a higher player count from both Corporate and Personal decks, shuffle separately, then deal each player one of each before Character draft. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the rejected card face down, unseen by anyone. Eggs do not trigger this choice; only an Intruder miniature appearing does.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments: 'first time an Intruder miniature ... appears'; 'Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.'

answers.answer: Discard the played Action card and two additional Action cards to pay its cost of 2. The two Contamination cards cannot pay Action costs. For a card with OR sections, choose one section.
answers.evidence: Actions: an Action card is discarded and its cost is paid with the required number of additional Action cards; Contamination cards can never pay; for OR choose one.

answers.answer: They take 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, including a round in which they take one Action and pass. Once passed, they cannot take further Actions this Player Phase. They may discard any number of hand cards when passing. Later players' rounds do not make this Character take Fire damage again that turn.
answers.evidence: Player rounds: a Character ending their round in a Room with Fire suffers 1 Light Wound; passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn; passing prevents further Actions and permits discarding any number of cards.

answers.answer: On entering an unexplored Room, flip its tile face up and reveal its Exploration token; orient the tile so the token's item number faces the Item Counter, then resolve its effect and remove the token. If the Room is empty, roll Noise; if a Character or Intruder is already there, do not roll. Silence suppresses the roll; with Slime it becomes Danger. Danger suppresses the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, places Noise in every connected corridor without a marker. On Noise results 1–4, place the marker in the correspondingly numbered connected Corridor (including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance); if that Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead. The marker is not placed if Silence resolves; Danger places markers in every eligible connected Corridor only when there are no eligible Intruders.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. It is forbidden in Combat and if all destination-connected Corridors already have Noise. Closed Doors block passage; a miniature cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement cost/restrictions; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: Closed Door blocks neighboring status and no one may stop in a Corridor.

answers.answer: If the roll's numbered Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead of placing another marker. With a Technical Corridors Entrance, the Technical Corridor is included and the Noise marker goes on the shared Technical Corridors space. For an Encounter, discard all Noise in Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance), draw a token, and place its matching miniature. Set the drawn token aside outside the bag; it may return if an Intruder of that type later hides in the Technical Corridors. Compare its number to the triggering player's hand size: Action and Contamination cards both count; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack. Contamination cards count in that comparison.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters: remove connected Noise, draw/place token, and compare token number to Action AND Contamination cards in triggering player's hand.

answers.answer: Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character into the Room. If none are eligible, place Noise in each connected Corridor without a marker (including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). An Intruder moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. Slime changes a Silence result into Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens and Noise roll: Danger moves all eligible Intruders, otherwise places markers; Encounters: an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; Slime marker rule.

answers.answer: A Blank drawn during an Encounter places Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room; no miniature appears. If it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available, then return the Blank. During bag development, a Blank adds an Adult token if available and is returned; no Room Encounter is described for that development draw.
answers.evidence: Encounters, 'Blank token in an Encounter'; Event Phase, Intruder bag development, Blank result.

answers.answer: Intruders trying to move through a Closed Door destroy it and stay in their starting Room. If several attempt through the same Door together, they destroy it simultaneously and all stay. A Destroyed Door cannot later be closed again, except with the Plasma Torch. An Intruder appearing due to a Noise roll can come through a Corridor with a Closed Door; the Door does not block that appearance.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers: Closed Door movement, simultaneous movement, destroyed-door rule, and Noise appearance exception.

answers.answer: An Intruder moving to a Technical Corridors Entrance disappears: remove its miniature, discard all Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. Noise on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors (only the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item are exceptions); Doors cannot be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors section: Intruder disappearance and Character exceptions; Noise marker remains; Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Shoot costs 1 Action card, requires a Hand weapon with ammo, targets one Intruder in the Character's Room, and discards 1 Ammo. It draws no Contamination card. A blank Combat die result misses without the Melee miss penalty; a two-hit result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting, before Weapon modifications. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto the Action discard pile, and targets one Intruder in the same Room. A miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound on the Character, and the two-hit result deals only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Combat: Shoot and Melee Attack procedures and results; Contamination cards section: received Contamination is placed on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: A Larva or Egg dies from 1 Injury; remove its miniature and do not place a Carcass. For Creeper or Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and kill it if the blood value is equal to or lower than its current injuries; place a Carcass. For Queen or Breeder, draw two and add the blood values, using the same comparison; place a Carcass if killed. During an Injury Effect check, a Retreat arrow makes the Intruder flee along the Corridor number on a drawn Event card; a Queen or Breeder retreats if either of its two cards has the arrow.
answers.evidence: Combat, Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room, targeting the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room; if it is empty, resolve a Noise roll, and if unexplored, explore it normally.
answers.evidence: Combat, Character Escape.

answers.answer: With several Characters in the Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder or next player in turn order. Draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching attacker symbol triggers its effect, otherwise the attack misses. A Larva instead removes its miniature from the board, places it on the target's Character board, and gives the target a Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards section.

answers.answer: Dressing a Serious Wound does not prevent death from another Wound at three Serious Wounds: dressing ignores the card's effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as specified by the healing effect. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death: three Serious Wounds plus any Wound kills; dressing still counts; Light Wound conversion; Heal; death and dropped objects.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan Contamination cards in the Character's hand only, removing all non-Infected cards; an Infected result places a Larva, and if one is already present the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower also removes Slime. Surgery scans cards in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, removes a Larva if present, then causes 1 Light Wound and an automatic pass. Shuffle all cards, including the hand and remaining Contamination cards, into the Action deck; the hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions, Canteen/Shower/Surgery; Contamination cards section.

answers.answer: In a Room with uncarried Eggs, use Shoot or Melee against them; each Injury of any type destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination, and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov destroys 1. Roll Noise after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. Fire in the Room destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with an Injury marker. The summary gives no further Melee penalties to waive beyond the no-Contamination and no-miss-Wound rules stated here.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: destroying Eggs and Nest destruction.

answers.answer: Enter using the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards) if the Pod is Unlocked and has a free Character space. Make a Noise roll first; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present in the Room, and the Room Actions reference also lists a Malfunction token as preventing entry. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. After entry, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit voluntarily for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Room while waiting, all pod occupants return to that Room; another Character entering your Pod may launch it immediately.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods section and Room Actions, Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: Victory checks are Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. If two or three Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes; hibernating Characters die. If the destination is not Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. An infected survivor scans all Contamination cards in deck, discard pile, and hand; if at least one is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four, dying if any Contamination card appears among them. A survivor carrying a Larva skips the scan step and resolves the draw-four test directly. Evacuated pod survivors are included in the Contamination check, so they do need that check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination; applies to each surviving Character 'hibernating or evacuated.'
